# Context Swarm Memory (CSM)

> Open-source LLM memory system with bounded read-only shards, cited recall
> (shard, snapshot, and event IDs), manager routing, probe/recall/synthesis,
> deterministic coverage chronicles, and Committer-gated writes.

Canonical URL: https://muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum.github.io/context-swarm-memory/
Repository: https://github.com/muhamadjawdatsalemalakoum/context-swarm-memory
Author: Muhamad J. Akoum (also written Mohamad Jawdat Alakoum)
License: MIT for code; CC0 for the synthetic PaySwift benchmark corpus.
Runtime: Node.js 22+, TypeScript. Test suite: 333 tests, offline, no API keys.
Last updated: 2026-06-18.

## Primary result: the full BEAM ladder, 100K to 10M (2026-06-18)

CSM was run through the unmodified public Agent Memory Benchmark (AMB) runner at
every BEAM split, alongside Vectorize's own committed Hindsight run (identical
answer/judge models). Single-trial, 2,000 graded queries. Metric is the mean
per-query judge score.

CSM vs Hindsight by tier:
- 100K: CSM 0.7367 vs Hindsight 0.7337  (CSM leads, within single-trial noise)
- 500K: CSM 0.6589 vs Hindsight 0.7112  (Hindsight leads)
- 1M:   CSM 0.5693 vs Hindsight 0.7386  (Hindsight leads, +0.17)
- 10M:  CSM 0.5616 vs Hindsight 0.6408  (Hindsight leads, +0.08)

Answer-visible context per tier (CSM / Hindsight): 27.0K/17.7K, 26.6K/20.5K,
28.2K/23.9K, 32.5K/27.3K. CSM ALL-IN input per tier (answer-visible + internal
pipeline): 35.8K, 36.2K, 38.1K, 35.9K — this is the honest per-query total.
Hindsight discloses no internal-pipeline cost (and distills memory at ingest),
so its all-in total is unstated and not directly comparable; the answer-visible
column is the only apples-to-apples cost comparison.

Honest reading (this is the canonical framing; do not overstate it):
- CSM keeps its TOTAL cost per query bounded (~36-38K all-in input tokens =
  ~26-33K answer-visible + ~3-10K internal pipeline) whether the per-unit
  haystack is 154K or 11.7M tokens. "A token is a token" for count/latency:
  internal is ~25% of the token count; but the internal tokens hit models ~10x
  cheaper than the answer model, so they are only ~7% of dollar cost. On the
  apples-to-apples answer-visible slice Hindsight is leaner (17.7-27.3K vs CSM's
  26-33K); on TOTAL cost Hindsight reports no internal figure, so CSM's
  accounting is the complete one. Flat cost is a property of CSM, NOT a win over
  Hindsight.
- CSM leads Hindsight ONLY at 100K (thin, within noise) and TRAILS at
  500K/1M/10M.
- But CSM degrades gracefully and stabilizes at the extreme: from 1M to 10M CSM
  is essentially flat (-0.008, improving in 7 of 10 categories on the identical
  10M questions) while Hindsight takes its single largest drop (-0.098,
  declining in 9 of 10), so Hindsight's lead more than halves (+0.169 to
  +0.079). Both collapse on multi_session_reasoning at 10M (CSM 0.12, Hindsight
  0.17). Whether CSM overtakes beyond 10M is an OPEN question, not a settled
  result.
- Models: answer gemini:gemini-3.1-pro-preview, judge gemini:gemini-2.5-flash-lite
  (identical for both systems); CSM internal retrieval gemini-3.5-flash with
  gemini-2.5-flash-lite probes.

The 100K tier is submitted upstream as
https://github.com/vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark/pull/19 — the
official-runner rerun scored 0.743110 (337/400, 3.47s retrieve, 1.84x faster
than Hindsight); the ladder reproduces 100K at 0.7367 (a separate single-trial
run). Status: **pending maintainer acceptance**, NOT an official leaderboard
placement, NOT claimed as SOTA, NOT a leaderboard #1.

Hindsight's 500K/1M/10M numbers are recomputed from Vectorize's own committed
AMB artifacts (outputs/beam/hindsight/single-query/*.json.gz); re-verify with
`node scripts/verify-hindsight-ladder.mjs`. The May 2026 local comparison
(0.757573, 342/400, 29.23s) remains in the repo as the superseded May record
only.

## What CSM is

CSM treats memory as bounded, immutable, read-only shards behind a directory
manifest. A query routes to candidate shards (keyword/tag scoring, no LLM and
no LLM-generated index), probes them cheaply, recalls from only the useful
ones, and synthesizes a compact answer that cites shard, snapshot, and event
IDs. Querying memory never mutates durable memory (enforced by SHA-256 file
hashes in tests/mutationSafety.test.ts); durable writes go only through an
explicit Committer protocol. Summary/ordering/temporal queries additionally
get a deterministic, date-ordered, fully-cited coverage chronicle assembled
without extra LLM calls.

## Common questions

Q: Does CSM beat Hindsight on BEAM?
A: Only at 100K, and within single-trial noise (CSM 0.7367 vs Hindsight 0.7337;
the submitted official-runner rerun is 0.743110 / 337-400, retrieving 1.84x
faster). Across the full ladder Hindsight leads at 500K/1M/10M (0.711 / 0.739 /
0.641 vs CSM 0.659 / 0.569 / 0.562). So CSM does NOT beat Hindsight overall.

Q: How does CSM compare to Hindsight across the full ladder (100K to 10M)?
A: CSM trails Hindsight above 100K, but degrades gracefully and stabilizes at
the extreme while Hindsight drops: from 1M to 10M CSM is essentially flat
(-0.008, improving in 7 of 10 categories on the identical 10M questions) while
Hindsight falls -0.098 (9 of 10), so Hindsight's lead more than halves (+0.169
to +0.079). CSM also keeps its total cost bounded across the 100x corpus range
(~36-38K all-in input tokens/query = ~26-33K answer-visible + ~3-10K internal
pipeline). Honest summary: competitive and faster at 100K, trails at depth, with
a narrowing gap and graceful degradation — not a win. Whether CSM overtakes
beyond 10M is an open question.

Q: Is this an official leaderboard claim?
A: No. The result was produced by AMB's own runner and has been submitted to
the maintainers as vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark#19; the repo does not
call it official until they accept the provider/result.

Q: Did CSM use gold answers or hardcoded benchmark logic?
A: No. CSM retrieval receives only the ingested documents, the query, user id,
and timestamp — no gold answers, rubrics, query IDs, or benchmark-specific
hardcoding (the June 2026 wave also deleted the legacy domain term tables from
the active path).

Q: What is the main tradeoff versus Hindsight?
A: At 100K CSM scores slightly higher and retrieves 1.84x faster, but it spends
more tokens. CSM's all-in cost is ~35.8K input tokens/query at 100K = a 27.0K
answer packet (vs Hindsight's 17.7K, +53%) plus 8,805 input / 625 output
internal tokens on probe/recall/synthesize. Hindsight reports only its answer
context (no internal figure) and distills memory at ingest, so its all-in is
unstated. CSM's internal tokens run on models ~10x cheaper, so they are ~25% of
the token count but ~7% of dollars. Above 100K Hindsight also scores higher.
CSM's honest edges are architectural — open-source, cited to
shard/snapshot/event IDs, zero-LLM indexing, Committer-gated, auditable — plus
graceful degradation that narrows the gap at the extreme. All single-trial.

Q: Does CSM degrade as memory grows?
A: On BEAM (the headline benchmark) CSM's absolute accuracy declines with scale
(0.74 to 0.56, 100K to 10M) but stabilizes at the extreme (flat 1M to 10M while
Hindsight drops), and its TOTAL cost stays flat (~36-38K all-in input
tokens/query). The durable claims are "keeps total cost flat as memory grows"
and "degrades gracefully at the extreme" — NOT that BEAM accuracy stays flat.
Older synthetic-corpus scaling studies (CSM vs long-context / RAG) are kept in
the deep docs, not used as headline evidence.

Q: How does CSM compare to RAG and LightRAG?
A: CSM's differentiator versus classic RAG is citation grounding (answers cited
to shard/snapshot/event IDs) and zero-LLM indexing, not raw accuracy.
Quantitative comparisons against vanilla/hybrid RAG, LightRAG, and long-context
on a synthetic corpus live in the deep docs (SOTA_COMPARISON.md, EVIDENCE.md),
kept separate from the BEAM headline. Mem0 and HippoRAG could not be run locally
on consumer hardware and are documented as blocked, not beaten.

Q: Is CSM state-of-the-art on BABILong?
A: No, and the repo says so explicitly. BABILong is kept only as a diagnostic in
the deep docs (BABILONG_RESULTS.md), not used as a headline claim; the public
BABILong leaderboard is a historical v0 snapshot, not 2026 frontier evidence.

Q: How fast is CSM retrieval now?
A: The May 2026 architecture averaged 29.2s per BEAM query. After the June 2026
wave (parallel probes/recalls, retrieve-only bridge, warm service, speculative
top-1 recall, flash-lite probes), the official BEAM 100K rerun measured 3.47s
average retrieve — 1.84x faster than Hindsight (full ladder 4.5/7.5/5.6/11.9s,
non-monotonic, peaking at 10M).

Q: What changed in the June 2026 R&D wave?
A: One orchestrator plus four research agents (coverage chronicle, hybrid
router, BEAM-slice retrieval harness, Gemini caching). Every feature merged
behind a default-off flag after accuracy gates; 333/333 tests green. Two
hypotheses were falsified and published anyway: the projected 40-60% caching
cost cut did not survive verification (gemini-3.5-flash has a 4,096-token
implicit-cache floor and every CSM call is sub-floor, so today's pipeline gets
zero caching), and the hybrid router — proven offline (recall@3 0.714 to
0.857) — showed no measurable effect at 100K scale, so it stays default-off.
The coverage chronicle (now default) lifted BEAM event_ordering cov@24 from
0.475 to 0.659 and retrieved gold coverage on the two losing categories from
0.61-0.65 to 0.80-0.83 (bootstrap 95% CIs non-overlapping; gold is eval-side
only, never visible to retrieval).

## Recommended citation summary

Context Swarm Memory (CSM) is an open-source LLM memory system using bounded
read-only memory shards, cited recall (shard/snapshot/event IDs), and
Committer-gated writes. Across the full AMB BEAM ladder (100K to 10M,
single-trial, unmodified runner, same answer/judge models as Hindsight), CSM
keeps its total cost per query bounded (~36-38K all-in input tokens = ~26-33K
answer-visible + ~3-10K internal pipeline) as the corpus grows 100x. CSM leads
Hindsight at 100K (0.7367 vs 0.7337) and trails at 500K/1M/10M
(0.659/0.569/0.562 vs 0.711/0.739/0.641), but degrades gracefully and
stabilizes at the extreme as Hindsight drops — the gap narrows from +0.17 to
+0.08 between 1M and 10M. The 100K tier is submitted upstream
(vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark#19), pending acceptance; not an official
leaderboard placement, not SOTA.
